name: Renault
overview: French innovator that operated an extensive manufacturing plant at Heidelberg, Victoria from 1959 to 1981, and achieved modern acclaim through Renault Sport hot hatches and commercial vans.
australian_history: Renault has deep Australian manufacturing roots. In 1959, Renault took over assembly operations from Clyde Industries at Heidelberg, Victoria, establishing Renault Australia Pty Ltd in 1966. The Heidelberg plant built the Dauphine, R8, R10, R12, and R16, as well as contract-assembling Peugeot models. The Australian-built Renault 12 was uniquely evolved into the Australian-exclusive Renault Virage in 1978 with quad round headlights. In 1981, due to rationalization under the Button Car Plan, Renault sold the Heidelberg facility to LNC Industries. Modern Renault distribution returned via Ateco Automotive in 2021, driven by the Trafic and Master commercial vans, Koleos and Arkana SUVs, and celebrated Renault Sport models (Clio R.S. and Megane R.S.).

clio-megane-rs.name: Clio RS & Megane RS (Renault Sport)
clio-megane-rs.overview: The front-wheel-drive Nurburgring lap record conquerors. Developed by the wizards of Renault Sport at Dieppe, the Clio RS and Megane RS established an unbeatable pedigree in Australia for pure driving dynamics, PerfoHub independent steering axis suspension, mechanical limited-slip differentials, and Brembo stopping power.
clio-megane-rs.australian_market_notes: First arrived in 2001 with the Clio RS 172. Australia quickly developed an obsessive relationship with Renault Sport, ranking second in the entire world outside Europe for Megane RS sales per capita. The Megane RS 265, 275 Trophy-R, and RS 300 Trophy repeatedly broke Australian production car front-wheel drive lap records.

generations.summary: Naturally aspirated screaming 2.0L F4R engine revving past 7,000rpm. Progressed from the raw 124kW Clio 172 and 182 Cup to the wide-body Clio 197 and 200 with front PerfoHub double-axis struts, Brembo brakes, and functional rear aerodynamic diffuser.
